text:
alex_dev: Heads up — after the mixtral-moerouter kernel bump last night we're seeing a p99 spike on Mixtral-MoE routing workloads. Baseline qps looks fine but tail latency jumps under multi-tenant bursts. suspected: router->expert handoff and KV cache thrash causing soft backpressure.

ben_ml: Ooh. Saw similar in local repro. Quick notes: when top_k >= 8 the router emits a long tail of logits that causes many small expert dispatches. That amplifies KV cache misses and leads to repeated small kernel launches on the GPU. p99 goes up ~2.5x on our perf rig.

maria_infra: Do we have flamegraphs or kernel timelines from the perf job? Could also be kernel selection falling back to a slower softmax / scatter pattern.

ben_ml: I pulled the sampler trace:
```
2026-03-17 03:22:11 GPU0 kernel launch: mixtral.router_dispatch (ms: 0.42)
2026-03-17 03:22:11 GPU0 kernel launch: expert_forward_0 (ms: 1.3)
2026-03-17 03:22:11 GPU0 kernel launch: expert_forward_1 (ms: 1.29)
2026-03-17 03:22:11 GPU0 kernel launch: kv_read (ms: 0.9)  # lots of small kv reads
2026-03-17 03:22:11 GPU0 kernel launch: scatter_softmax (ms: 2.8)  # fallback path
```
Key is the `scatter_softmax` fallback — that's ~3x slower per token than the optimized kernel.

alex_dev: Hm. What triggered the fallback? Did the kernel-selector policy change? We pushed a heuristics tweak to prefer single-expert fused kernels for small batches. Maybe that heuristic misfires with high top_k.

sam_reliability: Also noticed higher PCIe PCIe transfers during bursts in the trace — suggests more frequent KV flushes. Could be our eviction policy TTL is too low for MoE access patterns.

ben_ml: Agreed. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) tighten router logits clipping to reduce very low-confidence expert candidates (normalize temperature / logits clipping), and 2) change batching heuristics to favor slightly larger per-expert micro-batches to amortize kernel overhead. Example config we tested locally: 
```json
{
  "router": {
    "top_k": 4,
    "logit_clip": 8.0,
    "temperature": 0.95
  },
  "batching": {
    "max_micro_batch": 128,
    "min_micro_batch": 24,
    "dynamic_window_ms": 8
  },
  "kv_cache": {
    "eviction_ttl_ms": 20000,
    "read_prefetch": true
  }
}
```
This dropped p99 ~35% in the lab for the same synthetic burst.

maria_infra: Nice. From infra side we should also adjust kernel selector thresholds so that the optimized scatter-fused softmax is chosen unless the expected per-expert payload < 16 tokens. Right now our threshold is 32 tokens which is too conservative for Mixtral's head/kdim shape.

alex_dev: Good call. Mixtral's head dims and k/v layout differ from Llama; our selector shouldn't reuse defaults. @ben_ml can you run an A/B with lower threshold? Also let's instrument the router with a histogram of per-call expert payload sizes so selector gets live feedback.

ben_ml: On it. I'll add a quick metric: `router.expert_payload_tokens{model=mixtral}` and a trace tag for `kernel_choice`. Should have numbers in ~30m.

sam_reliability: Also thinking about expert parallelism — if certain hot experts are saturating, enabling expert-sharding across two worker streams (parallelism factor 2) reduces per-expert queueing and may improve tail. Tradeoff is slightly higher memory reuse and cross-stream sync. This could be toggled per-model.

alex_dev: Let's not flip expert parallelism globally. Plan: 1) canary rollout with config changes (top_k 4, logit_clip 8.0, micro-batch tuning, kv ttl bump), 2) lower kernel-selector token-threshold to 16 for mixtral model family, 3) enable expert-parallelism=2 for the canary if p99 remains high.

maria_infra: Canary command: `redwoodctl rollout apply mixtral-moerouter:v2 --canary 5% --config=canary-mixtral-20260317.json` — I'll wire CI to run the perf-suite against the canary slice.

ben_ml: Perf suite will include `perf/mixtral_moe_topk_burst.yml` — it stresses high topk and KV churn. I'll add an assertion for `router.kernel_choice` to ensure we don't hit the scatter fallback frequently.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for mixtral-moerouter:v2 -> 5% of routing traffic. Jobs queued: perf-suite, canary-observe.

sam_reliability: When canary finishes, please paste the `router.expert_payload_tokens` histogram and `kernel_choice` counts. If we still see >10% fallback to scatter kernels under burst load, we should automatically clip logits harder and reduce top_k to 3 for that traffic slice. :warning:

alex_dev: Agreed. Thanks all — let's reconvene after the canary results.

maria_infra: I'll also add a quick dashboard tile for KV cache hit rate per-model so we can correlate hit-rate with p99.

ben_ml: FYI local quick numbers: before change: p99=210ms, after change: p99=136ms, kv-hit-rate +8%. Will paste full traces when canary completes.

ci-bot: perf-suite: job mixtral_moe_topk_burst started (job-id: 20260317-78).
